messages.content: Summarize this documentation excerpt in three sentences: repeated to length, 256 greedy tokens. | Context | KV | Prompt | Decode after | Peak VRAM | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 128K | int8 | 888 tok/s (144 s) | 66.6 tok/s | 29.9 GB | | 128K | q4_0 | 848 tok/s | 62.8 tok/s | 29.7 GB | | 128K | k8v4, KV in VRAM | 1,006 tok/s | 66.8 tok/s | 30.7 GB | | 256K | int8 | 757 tok/s (338 s) | 55.9 tok/s | 30.2 GB | | 256K | q4_0 | 737 tok/s | 51.7 tok/s | 30.0 GB | | 256K | k8v4, KV in VRAM | 823 tok/s | 52.2 tok/s | 30.9 GB | Borrowing keeps every expert in VRAM (the prompt buffers live in lent cache slots, refilled after the prompt). Without it (`--no-prefill-borrow`) about 1,000-2,300 experts move to the pinned host mirror: the prompt is 2-5% faster and decode after it 10-23% slower. ## Arc Pro B70 with a model that does not fit: Flash-Next IQ3_S IQ3_S has 24,576 experts of 1.97 MB (46 GB). The 32 GB card holds about 11.5k of them (22 GiB of cache) and the rest sit in a pinned host mirror that the GPU reads over PCIe. Every prompt chunk streams the experts the cache does not hold, so a 4K prompt moves about 26 GB; bigger chunks read faster. - `setup_intel.py` writes `--prefill 4096` for a card with 24 GB or more (the chunk's buffers take about 700 cache slots). `--prefill 8192 --prefill-borrow` lends cache slots instead and keeps all of them for decode, at about 1 s of refill per prompt. Setup recommends 8,192 for a Battlemage card with 24 GB or more above 32K context. - `STRATA_PREFILL_FIRST` (a short first chunk that starts the GPU while PLE rows are read) defaults to 256 tokens only when the cache holds every expert, else 0. - `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=1` is required whenever part of the experts is not in VRAM (`strata-sycl.sh` sets it). Without it the host/GPU handshake is not visible across the bus on `xe` and the logits turn NaN a few tokens in. - On `xe`, setup writes `terminal/data/expert-profile-sycl.bin`, a ranking built from the routing of 45 varied prompts, so the cache holds the experts a chat, code or non-English prompt uses (`terminal/tools/make_profile_mix.py`, `terminal/tools/collect_profile_traces.py`). An `i915` card keeps the shipped profile. - The prompt's expert copies run on the card's copy engine on Battlemage (`STRATA_COPY_ENGINE=1` forces it elsewhere, `=0` turns it off). The experts in the last 10% of the cache slots are also mirrored so that lent slots refill by DMA (`STRATA_LEND_MIRROR=0` off). > **Measured on:** Arc Pro B70 32 GB (xe, kernel 7.0, oneAPI 2026.1, PCIe 13.3 GB/s host to device), 60 GB RAM, Flash-Next IQ3_S, > 11.5k experts resident, greedy, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp`, INT8 KV, `--stream-experts --vram-reserve-mib 1024 > --ple-io ram`, engine 0.1.40-sycl to 0.1.43. The 10-prompt `mg_norepeat` gate passes 10 of 10. | Workload | Result | | --- | --- | | 4,095-token prompt, `--prefill 4096` | 980-1,002 tok/s | | 8,169-token prompt, `--prefill 8192` lending cache slots | 1,117 tok/s (9.4k slots) | | Decode, 200-token story (66% of drafts accepted) | 30.5 tok/s | | Decode, 200-token code answer (90% accepted) | 40.8 tok/s | | 128K config, 4K prompt incl. refill (0.1.43) | 3.3 s (was 7.2 s); 16K 13.5 s (was 25.5); 49K 44 s (was 78) | | `--prefill 8192` against 4096, 16K / 32K prompt (IQ3_S, setup's 128K flags) | 1,347-1,362 against 1,222 tok/s (+10-11%); 1,361-1,383 against 1,187 (+15-16%); decode after unchanged | | Fused int8 expert prompt path (`auto`) against FP16 chain, 1,024 / 4,095 tokens | 783.5 against 645.8 (+21%); 1,407.7 against 1,257.0 (+12%) | Draft length (200 tokens, `--spec-min-p 0.5`): `--spec 6` against `--spec 4` is +6.5% on code and -1.5% on prose, so the setup default (4, 0.5) stays. A `--prefill 8192` chunk is not bit-identical to 4096 (first-token KL 1.1e-2 at 16K, top-1 the same). **Fused int8 expert path (Battlemage default).** On a Battlemage GPU (B70, B580, B570, detected by device architecture) the engine computes the prompt's routed experts with ESIMD kernels that decode the quantized weights in registers into the s8 DPAS B operand and multiply them by q8_1 activations. Covered: gate/up IQ3_S, IQ3_XXS, IQ2_S and down IQ4_NL, Q2_0. Other formats keep the FP16 path, as does every other GPU. `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ` unset is `auto`, which times both chains at the first layer of each format and takes int8 below the measured crossover (130-250 rows per expert); `=0` turns it off, `=1` forces it. Activations are quantized, so bits differ from the FP16 path (KL 2e-4 nats mean over 6,002 positions, top-1 99.7%). Details: [INTEL_INT8_EXPERTS.md](INTEL_INT8_EXPERTS.md). ## Arc A750 and the other Alchemist cards An Alchemist card (A750, A770 and so on) has no FP64 hardware, and the A750 runs on the `i915` driver. `./setup.sh --backend sycl` writes a different config for an `i915` card, and a 300 MiB VRAM reserve and `--draft-vocab en` for any card under 12 GB. | | Arc Pro B70 (`xe`, 32 GB) | Arc A750 (`i915`, 8 GB) | | --- | --- | --- | | Experts | `--stream-experts`: from the GGUF into VRAM, the rest in a pinned RAM mirror | No `--stream-experts`: all of them in a RAM arena (about 40 GiB for IQ3_XXS), a few hundred in VRAM, the CPU computes the others | | `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST` | 1 (the wrapper's default) | 0, written to the config's `"env"` | | `--vram-reserve-mib` | 1024 / 2048 | 300 | | `--ple-io` | `ram` | `ram` | | FP64 | Native | Emulated: `IGC_EnableDPEmulation=1`, `OverrideDefaultFP64Settings=1`, `NEOReadDebugKeys=1` in `"env"` | | Build | AOT `bmg-g31` | JIT (no `AOT=`) | - **Why no `--stream-experts` on the A750.** The mirror is one pinned host allocation, and a single `sycl::malloc_host` above a few GB fails on the A750. Without the flag the engine loads the experts into an ordinary RAM arena and the CPU computes the experts that are not in the 0.67 GiB cache. That needs about 43 GB of RAM for IQ3_XXS plus the 29 GB n-gram table with `--ple-io ram`. Setup warns when the RAM is less than the model's. - **Why `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=0`.** With it set the GPU plans each layer itself and the CPU's experts are never asked for; the window hangs (`Fence expiration time out` in the i915 log). - **FP64.** One kernel on the sampled path declared `double`; the sampler's tail now accumulates in float (`-DSTRATA_SYCL_SAMPLER_FP64=1` keeps double). Setup still writes the three emulation keys for an A-series card, because other kernels that use double were not exercised without them on long contexts or with vision. On the A750 a sampled decode ran at 12.0 tok/s without the emulation keys against 9.8 with them (median of 4 interleaved pairs). - **Prompt GDN recurrence** runs a sub-group kernel on Alchemist (variant 6, `STRATA_GDN_XE`): on by default there, `=0` off, `=1` on any Intel GPU with 16-lane sub-groups. On Battlemage it stays off (-3.5%). - **Grouped XMX expert launch** (`STRATA_PF_XMX=2`) is the default on Alchemist: the prompt path decodes and multiplies a group of experts in one fused launch on the XMX units. `=0` turns it off; `=1` dequantizes first and runs one grouped GEMM per product. Battlemage keeps the older path (the same kernels are 7-11% slower there). - **Streaming copies.** Only experts in USM host memory (the `--stream-experts` mirror) are copied directly; every other expert goes through the stager's pinned buffers, because SYCL has no `cudaHostRegister` and a direct copy out of pageable memory could hang a prompt. `STRATA_PF_DMA_PAGEABLE=1` restores the direct copy. - The engine segfaults in a worker thread of the CPU pool when it exits (dmesg only, after the server printed "stopped"). It is not a GPU event. > **Measured on:** Arc A750 8 GB (i915, PCIe 4.0), Ryzen 5 5600X (AVX2, no AVX-512), 64 GB RAM, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, default > flags, engine 0.1.45.3. | Workload | Result | | --- | --- | | Prompt, 1K / 2K / 4K / 6K tokens, grouped XMX launch | 46.4 / 83.1 / 110.4 / 114.8 tok/s (before: 35.1 / 61.7 / 79.3 / 66.3) | | Decode | 18.7 tok/s (unchanged by the grouped launch); 10-15 tok/s in the first report | | PCIe probe | 10.6 GB/s | | Quality of the grouped launch against the default | teacher-forced KL 0.0002 over 6,006 tokens (default against itself 0.0001), first-token KL 0.0017, top-1 99.7%; HumanEval (every 2nd, 82) 73, 69, 74; needles at 2K-6K 9/9; 8K-context tool-call agent 6/6 | **Gyro on an Arc.** Gyro-S and Gyro-M (trellis-coded experts, [GYRO.md](GYRO.md#intel-arc-sycl)) run on the SYCL engine. They were tested on the A750 only. Setup writes the usual A750 config (32K context, 300 MiB reserve) without `--ple-io ram`, because the 28 GB n-gram table stays on the SSD while the expert arena takes 24 GB of RAM (Gyro-S). Gyro-M needs `--max-context 8192 --vram-reserve-mib 100 --prefill 1024` on 8 GB. A second Arc card does not take Gyro's experts (the engine refuses and says so). The Battlemage AOT build compiles with the trellis kernels and was not run. > **Measured on:** Arc A750 (i915, 8 GB), Ryzen 5 5600X, 62 GB RAM, Gyro-S, engine version not recorded. | Workload | Result | | --- | ---: | | Prompt, 1,406 tokens | 82 tok/s (40 with dequantize + oneMKL) | | Prompt, 2,377 / 20,000 tokens | 102 / 195 tok/s | | Decode, MTP draft of 4 | 15-16 tok/s | | Experts in the card's cache | 410 of 24,576 | | Gyro-M, 8K context | decode 14 tok/s, prompt 62 tok/s | Decode is bound by the CPU pool and the PCIe link (10.4 GB/s), not by the card's kernels. `--prefill 1024` gave +13% decode and -24% prompt speed; the default stays `--prefill auto`. ## Pictures on an Arc Pictures follow the rule of every other card ([MODELS.md](MODELS.md#the-versions)): the picture reader runs on the CPU under 24 GB of VRAM and on the card from 24 GB. `terminal/strata_control/vision_reader.py` is the one place for that rule. On an Arc, pictures are on by default with the CPU reader, a B-series card included. An Arc of 24 GB or more also keeps the CPU reader; `--vision gpu` asks for the GPU reader. - **CPU reader:** `strata-vision` (Strata's own reader). Setup compiles it into `engine-sycl/`, the server runs it on the host, and the engine in the container reads the embeddings from the host's `/dev/shm`, which `strata-sycl.sh` shares (`STRATA_SYCL_SHM=0` keeps a private one). - **SYCL reader:** `strata-vision-sycl`, the same program on llama.cpp's SYCL backend. `setup --backend sycl --vision gpu` compiles it on the host when the oneAPI compiler (`icx`, `icpx`, `intel-oneapi-mkl-devel`) is installed; otherwise setup says so and keeps the CPU reader. It needs the PC's oneAPI runtime, not the container. If it does not start, the server falls back to the CPU reader with one log line. It takes VRAM the experts would use, which is why the rule gives it to 24 GB cards only. Nobody has run it on a card of 24 GB or more. - **Known risk on Battlemage.** The first picture on the Arc Pro B70 (engine 0.1.45, IQ3_S, CPU reader) logged an xe engine reset (ccs + bcs) and `Fault response: Unsuccessful -EINVAL`, and the request ended 503. It has not been looked at since. Setup and `strata launch` print one plain line that the card is new to Strata and how to report a problem. `--vision no` (setup) or `--vision off` (`strata launch`) turns pictures off. > **Measured on:** Arc A750 (8 GB), IQ3_XXS, 8K context, JIT build, 448x448 picture. | Reader | Time per picture | | --- | ---: | | CPU (`strata-vision`) | 1.73 s | | SYCL (`strata-vision-sycl`), after a 30 s first start that compiles the kernels | 0.16 s | The embeddings match the CPU reader's (cosine 0.9959 to 0.9999 over 8 pictures). A test picture (red circle, blue square, the words "STRATA 42") was answered correctly by both readers 10 of 10; two pictures in one request, a picture kept in a second turn's history, and text requests after the pictures all answered, with no GPU fault in the kernel log. ## The SYCL port (`sycl/`) **Layout.** `engine/sycl/src` and `engine/sycl/include` mirror the tree and hold only the files the port changes; `engine/sycl/CMakeLists.txt` takes every other source from the original location. `sycl/include/dpct/` is the vendored SYCLomatic helper library. **How it is made, so it can be redone.** 1. `engine/sycl/tools/Dockerfile` is the dev image: the llama.cpp SYCL image plus SYCLomatic (`dpct` 2025.3), ninja, and the CUDA 12.8 headers that `engine/sycl/tools/get-cuda-headers.sh` pulls from NVIDIA's pip wheels (dpct parses CUDA; it needs headers, not the toolkit). 2. `engine/sycl/tools/migrate.sh` writes a compilation database for the CUDA-touching translation units and runs dpct over them. 3. `engine/sycl/tools/fixups.py` fixes what dpct got wrong, as an idempotent script with a reason per item. Examples: CUDA's null stream becomes the default stream (every stream cast goes through `strata::q_of()`), `__ldg` and `__fadd_rn` translations that lost their meaning, ggml lookup tables as plain `static const` arrays. 4. `engine/sycl/tools/build.sh` configures and builds with icpx inside the image. Two compiler flags are load-bearing: `-fp-model=precise` (icpx defaults to a fast model) and `-cl-fp32-correctly-rounded-divide-sqrt` for the device compiler. The Arc's fp32 divide is not correctly rounded by default, and Strata's quantizers are byte-exact against ggml through `amax / 127`. **What the port had to get right.** - Host-mapped flags: `volatile` device loads do not bypass the caches on Intel; system-scope atomics do. Host-to-device visibility during a kernel stays unreliable, which is why the all-resident path waits for the window instead. - 32-lane sub-groups (`-fsycl-default-sub-group-size=32`): the kernels are written for warps. - Synchronous copies: `cudaMemcpy` blocks, dpct's default-queue `memcpy` did not wait. - Stager and PLE waits: no host thread waits on a queue's event under the Level Zero v2 adapter; the copy queue writes a sequence number into page-locked host memory and the stager polls it. - Profiling: `engine/sycl/tools/Dockerfile.unitrace` builds the dev image with Intel's unitrace; `unitrace -d` around the engine plus `sycl/rank_kernels.py` gives device time per kernel. **Keeping up with upstream.** A merge of upstream `main` leaves the copies in `sycl/` behind wherever upstream touched a file they mirror. They are refreshed by re-migration: 1. Merge upstream. No shared file should conflict. Check that `engine/sycl/setup_intel.py --check` and `engine/sycl/serve/server_intel.py --engine mock` still run against the new `setup.py` and `server.py`. 2. Migrate the old upstream tree with `migrate.sh` into `sycl-base` and the merged tree into `sycl-new`. 3. Run `engine/sycl/tools/normalize.sh ` on both (dpct's file names, unchanged files, message serials, then `fixups.py`). 4. For every file present in both: `git merge-file sycl/F sycl-base/F sycl-new/F`. Copies dpct never produced (`verify.cpp`, `mtp.cpp`, `remote_experts.cpp`) take upstream's diff by hand; new parity tests are copied in and listed in `engine/sycl/CMakeLists.txt`. 5. A fixup whose pattern upstream changed shows up as a compile error; extend the fixup, re-run it, rebuild. Run a symbol audit (count the port's feature identifiers before and after). `engine/sycl/tools/merge_upstream.py` ports open upstream PRs ahead of upstream the same way. **Not ported.** Three kernels carry inline PTX (`mma.sync`, `ldmatrix`, `cp.async`): `qsa_prompt_attn`, `qsa_select`'s block scores and `native_qsa_score`. The SYCL build takes the "older card" fallback the CUDA build uses below sm_80. `qsa_prompt_attn` also has an XMX version (`STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_XMX=1`) that is correct but slower than the fallback. The ggml MMQ prefill path (`moe_mmq.cu`) is not built. `--peer-device` (a second GPU as an expert-cache tier) is stubbed and refuses with a message. The sm_90 thread-block-cluster sampler and QSA top-k have no SYCL counterpart. Images on the llama.cpp config are not wired; on the SYCL port they are ([Pictures](#pictures-on-an-arc)). ## Switch reference All are environment variables for the engine. Put them in the config's `"env"` block. Defaults are for the current engine. | Switch | Default | Effect | | --- | --- | --- | | `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST` | 1 (`strata-sycl.sh`); 0 on `i915` | See above | | `STRATA_MIRROR_MIB` | Free RAM less 4 GiB | Size of the pinned host mirror for experts without a VRAM slot. Set `0` on a layer split where the mirror would not be used. | | `STRATA_PF_XMX` | 2 on Alchemist | Grouped XMX expert launch; `0` off, `1` dequantize first | | `STRATA_GDN_XE` | On for Alchemist | Sub-group GDN recurrence | | `STRATA_COPY_ENGINE` | On for Battlemage | Expert copies on the copy engine | | `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ` | `auto` on Battlemage | Fused int8 prompt experts | | `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_ALL` | On when VRAM holds more than 90% of the (layer, expert) pairs | Copy every expert the cache does not hold, layer by layer; `=0` / `=1` force it | | `STRATA_PREFILL_FIRST` | 256 if the cache holds every expert, else 0 | Tokens in the short first prompt chunk | | `STRATA_LEND_MIRROR` | On | Mirror the experts in the last 10% of cache slots; `=0` off | | `STRATA_VERIFY_LEAN` | On | Decode graph without unanswered nodes; `=0` off | | `STRATA_FILL_SERIAL=1` | Off | The old serial expert-cache fill (the pipelined fill is the default) | | `STRATA_MMVQ_A2=0`, `STRATA_MMVQ_WIDE_32=0` | On | Restore the older matvec kernels | | `STRATA_MMVQ_LARGE_GRF` | On for Arc A-series | 256 registers per thread for the 2-8 column wide kernels | | `STRATA_Q6_PLANAR` | On | Q6_K output head and MTP head as planes (same bytes) | | `STRATA_ATTN_RS` | 2 | QSA prompt attention probability layout (bit-exact variants) | | `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1` | Off | Wide kernel for dense IQ3_S matrices: neutral on one B70 (decode -0.3%), the author reports gains on two cards | | `STRATA_EXPERT_SPLIT=1` | Off | Upstream's i-quant multi kernels (-11 to -16% decode here) | | `STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_XMX=1` | Off | joint_matrix prompt attention (-24% to -27% prompt on the B70) | | `STRATA_SYCL_GEMM_STAGE=1` | Off on Battlemage | Stage GEMM operands past 4 GiB | | `STRATA_I8_NO_ESIMD` | n/a | Compile-time: stubs for the int8
